subject: Switching Data sets based on two user inputs

messages.author: b8f5874429e73503
messages.subject: Switching Data sets based on two user inputs
parts:
I am trying to create an app which will show a person's stats. based on each month of the current year.  However, I am not sure how to write code that will switch data sets (ex. January data to February data) when a user selects a different month for a person.  I have tried using the switch function, but it did not switch the data when I select different months on the app.  Please see the following code: 

UI R:
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(plotrix)

OpenJ16 <- read.csv("CasesOpenedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ClosedJ16 <- read.csv("CasesClosedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
CallsHandledJ16 <- read.csv("CallsHandledJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
POCJ16 <- read.csv("PercentageofCasesJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OverJan16 <- read.csv("Overviewjan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  
  titlePanel(title = h1("Infinite Campus Agent Stats.", align="center")),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("year", "Year", c("2016")),
      br(),
      selectInput("month", "Month", c("January", "Febuary", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August","September","October","November","December")),
      br(),
      selectInput("agentNames", "Infinite Campus Agents", 
                  choices = c("Andrew Davis" = 1,"Paul Dibartolo" = 2, "Michael Folan" = 3, "Megan Murray" = 4, "Victor Paulson" = 5, "Caitlin Roth" = 6)),
      br(),
      radioButtons("color", "Select Color:", choices = c("Green", "Blue", "Orange", "Red", "Yellow", "Purple"), selected = "Green")
      ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(type = "tab",
                  tabPanel("Summary",tableOutput("summaryjan16")),
                  tabPanel("Cases Open", plotOutput("janOpen16")),
                  tabPanel("Cases Closed", plotOutput("janClosed16")),
                  tabPanel("Phone Calls", plotOutput("janCH16")),
                  tabPanel("Percentage of Cases",plotOutput("janPC16"),br(),plotOutput("janPC216"))
        
      )
    )
    
    )
  )
)

Server R:
library(shiny)
library(plotrix)

OpenJ16 <- read.csv("CasesOpenedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ClosedJ16 <- read.csv("CasesClosedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
CallsHandledJ16 <- read.csv("CallsHandledJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
POCJ16 <- read.csv("PercentageofCasesJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OverJan16 <- read.csv("Overviewjan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

shinyServer(
  function(input, output, session)
  {
    output$janOpen16 <- renderPlot({
      colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
      barplot(OpenJ[,colm],breaks=seq(0, max(Open[,colm])), col = input$color, main = "Cases Opened in January", xlab = names(Open[colm]), ylab = "Cases Opened",names.arg = c("01/04","01/11","01/18","01/24"))
    })
    
    output$janCH16 <- renderPlot({
      colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
      plot(CallsHandledJ[,colm],type = "l",lwd=2, col = input$color,xlab = names(CallsHandledJ[colm]), ylab = "Calls Handled in January", main = "Calls Handled in January",ylim = c(0,40))
    })
  
  output$janClosed16 <- renderPlot({
    colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
    barplot(ClosedJ[,colm],breaks=seq(0, max(Open[,colm])), col = input$color, main = "Cases Closed in January", xlab = names(Open[colm]), ylab = "Cases Closed",names.arg = c("01/04","01/11","01/18","01/24"))
  })
  
  output$janPC16 <- renderPlot({
    colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
    pie3D(POCJ16[,colm],labels = names(Open[colm]),explode = 0.1, main = "Percentage of Cases Picked Up")
  })
  
  output$janPC216 <- renderPlot({
    pc <- c(22.6,10.16,20.11,13.57,9.78,22.25)
    lbls <- c("Andrew Davis","Paul DiBartolo","Michael Folan","Megan Murray","Victor Paulson","Caitlin Roth")
    pct <- round(pc/sum(pc)*100)
    lbls <- paste(lbls, pct)
    lbls <- paste(lbls,"%",sep="")
    pie(pc, labels = lbls, main = "Percentage of Cases Picked Up",col = rainbow(length(lbls)))
  })
  
  output$summaryjan16 <- renderTable(OverJan16)
    }
)

messages.author: ec79ef2df02af517
messages.subject: Re: Switching Data sets based on two user inputs
parts:
In server.R use input$month with an "if" statement:

if(input$month == "January") {

dataSet <- read.csv(CasesOpenedJan16.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

} else if (input$month == "February") {

dataSet <- read.csv(CasesOpenedFeb16.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

} else if (input$month %in% c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December") == TRUE) {

dataSet <- paste("You can't time travel to the future")

}

The variable dataSet will then be changed based on the selected value of input$month. 

I also don't think you need to load the csv files in ui.R. It'll save some time if you don't.
